pattern-selector.why: the forces are one fact (a hook path's repo-relative spelling) needed by three hooks; the fit is a single shared helper in the existing path owner, not a new abstraction, and the router stays a pure matcher. Rejected: normalizing inside the router, prefixing every glob with **/.
pattern-selector.what: added projectRoot/toRepoPath to esk-paths.mjs and called it from each hook; recorded the forces and alternatives in ADR-0104.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: where path conversion lives and what happens to a path outside the repo are decisions a future maintainer will ask about.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0104 with the decision, the pass-through reasoning, limits, and alternatives; validated with check_adr.sh.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the agent-facing behavior (an absolute-path edit to a routed folder is held) is a new edge case of the router scenario, so it gets an executable, tagged scenario in the datastore.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added the router-matches-absolute-edit-path scenario and its steps, regenerated the index, logged it; bdd-run and check-bdd-executed pass (96).
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the bug is in pure path logic plus three hooks, so it is caught with unit tests on toRepoPath and spawn tests on each real hook.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added unit tests for toRepoPath/projectRoot and hook tests for edit-gate, finish-check, subagent-check, transcript-files.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the edit-gate is a gate that was silently vacuous for root-anchored rules; its new tests must fail when the fix is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: replaced toRepoPath with the old separator-only behavior: 11 tests failed; restored. Absolute Windows-style and POSIX-style inputs both covered.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the fix rests on claims about what the hooks receive and what a wrong root does; each is stated with its limit (project dir is not the git root, cwd may differ per event, no POSIX host run).
skeptical-audit.what: wrote the limits into ADR-0104 and the PR, and checked the fail-open case (a wrong root never drops a file).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change restructures how three enforcement hooks name files, so it gets a fresh-context review over every changed code file.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context review (3 low findings), fixed all three, appended the review entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the simplest shape that meets the need: two small functions in the module that already owns hook paths, no git spawn per edit, no new module.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept the router pure and put conversion at the hook boundary.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the hook payload path is untrusted input to a control; the attack is a bypass where a path spelling dodges a required check. The conversion only narrows what passes (inside paths now match), never drops a path, and a bad root fails closed.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: outside or other-family paths pass through unchanged; a missing root blocks with its cause; tests cover sibling-prefix and other-drive paths.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, or hook registration change; the hooks keep the same wiring and contract. The one behavior tightening (root-anchored rules now fire) is called out in the changelog and ADR-0104.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: paths of edited files are operational data, not personal or regulated data; no retention or deletion duty changes.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service or endpoint; these are local hooks covered by tests.

arch-encode.why: the caught mistake (an absolute path matched against root-anchored globs) is not a source pattern arch-gate can grep for; it is pinned by discriminating tests instead.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; Node hooks only.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; hook messages stay plain-language and now name a bad root.
